local NS = 1e9
local sp = series("/nissan/vehicle_speed/data")
local gz = series("/nissan/gps/duro/imu/angular_velocity/z")
local az = series("/nissan/gps/duro/imu/linear_acceleration/z")

local function regions(s, pred, minDur, maxGap, opts)
  local start, last = nil, nil
  local n = s:size()
  for i = 0, n - 1 do
    local p = s:at(i)
    if pred(p) then
      if start == nil then start = p.t end
      last = p.t
    elseif start ~= nil and p.t - last > maxGap * NS then
      if last - start >= minDur * NS then
        startMarker(start)
        closeMarker(last, opts)
      end
      start, last = nil, nil
    end
  end
  if start ~= nil and last - start >= minDur * NS then
    startMarker(start)
    closeMarker(last, opts)
  end
end

-- stationary periods
regions(sp, function(p) return p.v < 0.3 end, 1.5, 0.5,
  {label = "Stopped", description = "vehicle speed < 0.3 m/s"})

-- hard braking: sustained decel >= 3 m/s^2 measured over a 0.6 s window of wheel speed
regions(sp, function(p)
  local v0 = sp:atTime(p.t - 0.6 * NS)
  if v0 == nil then return false end
  return (v0 - p.v) / 0.6 >= 3.0
end, 0.3, 0.4, {label = "Hard braking", description = "decel >= 3 m/s^2 over 0.6 s (from wheel speed)"})

-- hard cornering: |speed * yaw_rate| >= 3.5 m/s^2 sustained
regions(gz, function(p)
  local v = sp:atTime(p.t)
  if v == nil then return false end
  return math.abs(p.v * v) >= 3.5
end, 0.5, 0.4, {label = "Hard cornering", description = "|v * yaw_rate| >= 3.5 m/s^2"})

-- vertical jolts: specific force deviates > 4 m/s^2 from -g, clustered to one marker per second
local lastHit = nil
for i = 0, az:size() - 1 do
  local p = az:at(i)
  if math.abs(p.v + 9.93) > 4.0 then
    if lastHit == nil or p.t - lastHit > 1.0 * NS then
      createVerticalMarker(p.t, {label = "Vertical jolt", description = "|az + g| > 4 m/s^2 (road shock / bump)"})
    end
    lastHit = p.t
  end
end

-- top speed instant
local best, bt = -1, 0
for i = 0, sp:size() - 1 do
  local p = sp:at(i)
  if p.v > best then best, bt = p.v, p.t end
end
createVerticalMarker(bt, {label = string.format("Top speed %.1f m/s (%.0f km/h)", best, best * 3.6)})

Everything is in place and verified. Here's the full picture of the Nissan/ZalaZone log.

## What the drive looks like

A **231.5 s (3 min 51 s), 2.66 km** run in three distinct phases:

| Phase | Time | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Handling section | 0–65 s | Low speed (2–7 m/s) with large steering swings (−24° to +35°) — slalom/maneuvering, including near-stops around t≈27 s and t≈57 s |
| High-speed cruise | 65–180 s | Steady acceleration to a sustained 19–21 m/s (~70–75 km/h) with steering essentially at zero — a long straight. Top speed **20.97 m/s (75.5 km/h)** at t≈150 s |
| Slowdown + maneuver | 180–231 s | Gradual decel, a dip to ~6 m/s with renewed steering activity around 195–210 s (a turn or chicane), then final braking to a full stop |

## What I created (look in the **Custom Series** panel, bottom-left — drag onto plots)

- **`speed_kmh`** — vehicle speed in km/h (the raw signal is m/s).
- **`long_accel_from_speed`** — smoothed longitudinal acceleration derived from wheel speed (peaks: +6.9 / −3.5 m/s²). Much cleaner than the raw IMU x-axis, which is buried in ±1.5 m/s² of vibration.
- **`lat_accel_smooth`** — low-pass filtered IMU lateral acceleration (peaks ~±0.4 g).
- **`distance_traveled_m`** — integrated odometer; ends at **2664 m**.
- **`roll_deg` / `pitch_deg` / `yaw_deg`** — attitude in degrees (roll stays within −2.7°…+5.7°, pitch ±4.6°).
- **`yaw_rate_deg_s`** — gyro z in °/s (±41 °/s during the slalom).
- **`mag_field_norm_uT`** — magnetometer magnitude in µT.

Plus one **global marker set (12 markers, visible on every plot)**: shaded regions for *Stopped*, *Hard braking* (≥3 m/s² sustained 0.6 s), and *Hard cornering* (|v·ω| ≥ 3.5 m/s² sustained), vertical lines for 6 *Vertical jolt* road-shock events, and the top-speed instant.

## Things you should take into consideration

1. **The IMU acceleration is raw specific force, not gravity-compensated** — z averages −9.93 m/s². The negative sign on gravity also implies a z-down (or flipped-mount) axis convention; account for it before any fusion work.
2. **A violent shock at t≈185 s**: longitudinal acceleration swings −12.1…+9.2 m/s² within a fraction of a second while steering is straight and speed decays smoothly — that's a **bump/pothole hit at ~52 km/h**, not a driving maneuver. The jolt markers pinpoint it and five smaller ones.
3. **Magnetometer is plausible but disturbed**: mean norm 48.7 µT matches Earth's field in Hungary, but it excursions between 23 and 58 µT — hard/soft-iron interference from the vehicle. Don't trust magnetic heading during those dips.
4. **`current_pose` z is identically zero** — no altitude information; the x/y are local map-frame coordinates spanning ~1.6 × 1.8 km. Drag position/y vs position/x as an XY curve to see the track layout.
5. **Topics are on unsynchronized clocks/rates** (IMU 99 Hz, speed/steering 30 Hz, pose 20 Hz, mag 25 Hz) with no shared timestamps — I couldn't build a live speed×yaw-rate series for that reason; cross-signal event logic had to interpolate instead.
6. **The steering signal is likely road-wheel angle, not steering-wheel angle**: ±35° producing the observed yaw rates at low speed fits road-wheel geometry (a steering wheel would swing hundreds of degrees in a slalom).
7. **Driving style is moderate overall**: sustained deceleration never exceeded ~3.5 m/s², lateral acceleration ~0.4 g; the aggressive-looking raw IMU spikes are vibration, which is why all event detection required conditions to hold over time.
8. `/nissan/gps/duro/status_string` is a string topic I can't plot — it likely carries RTK/fix status; worth a manual look if you need to validate GPS quality during the run.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Deriving longitudinal acceleration from wheel speed (30 Hz, smooth) instead of the 99 Hz IMU is the right call here: the IMU x-axis has a σ of 1.5 m/s² from engine/road vibration, so a real 3 m/s² braking event barely clears its noise floor, while the wheel-speed derivative shows it cleanly.
- The one-marker-set constraint pushed all five detectors into a single rule — which is also the maintainable shape: shared region-merging logic (`minDur` + `maxGap`) keeps thresholds from spraying hundreds of per-sample markers.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
